Spring River at Hardy, AR — hydrologic regime 1981–2026

Base flow, floods, and precipitation over the Mammoth Spring recharge basin

Author

Spring River study (USGS 07069305 / NWS HDYA4)

Published

August 25, 2026

1 Abstract

Spring River at Hardy, AR (USGS 07069305) is a spring-fed Ozark river whose base flow is set by Mammoth Spring (07069190) and whose floods are set by basin rainfall. Over the systematic record (Hardy WY 2002–2026, Mammoth WY 1981–2026; 98.5% of Hardy daily discharge approved) the 7-day annual low flow at Hardy rose (Sen slope 0.023 log-cfs/yr (95% CI 0.00736 to 0.0361); MK z=3.05, p=0.002; n=24), but antecedent precipitation and ENSO explain it (OLS R² = 0.47, n = 24) and the non-climatic residual trend is indistinguishable from zero at both gauges (Mammoth Sen slope -0.00222 log-cfs/yr (95% CI -0.00497 to 0.000453); MK z=-1.71, p=0.087; n=42; Hardy Sen slope 0.00676 log-cfs/yr (95% CI -0.00135 to 0.0195); MK z=1.76, p=0.078; n=24). Base flow after the 6 major (≥16 ft) floods was higher, not lower, than in precipitation- and antecedent-matched non-flood years (Mammoth +27.5%, bootstrap 95% CI 19.8 to 42; Hardy +22.9%, CI 12.6 to 35.1; descriptive, not causal). The falling stage floor is largely a rating artifact: stage at 1000 cfs fell (Sen slope -0.0187 ft/yr (95% CI -0.0214 to -0.0157); MK z=-5.46, p=0.000; n=19). Flood frequency shows no detectable change: Imboden annual peaks Sen slope 0.00112 log10-cfs/yr (95% CI -0.00123 to 0.00406); MK z=0.94, p=0.346; n=89; the pre-/post-2008 10-yr quantiles (63,943 vs 95,546 cfs) have overlapping 5–95% bootstrap intervals. LP3 return periods at Hardy (n = 24) put 10 ft at 1.4 yr, 16 ft at 4.5 yr (empirical 4), 20 ft at 12.5 yr and 23 ft at 29 yr. Major-flood inter-arrivals are consistent with a memoryless process (CV 1.01, bootstrap p = 0.47, n = 7). Basin (PRISM) precipitation rose in 9/10 intensity indices (annual total +2.41 in/decade, 95% CI 0.35 to 4.5, n = 45; SDII +0.0347 in/wet-day/decade, CI 0.022 to 0.049) while the Sep–Feb recharge-season total is flat (-0.0177 in/decade, CI -1.3 to 1.2, n = 44). Monthly basin precipitation anomalies lead Mammoth Spring flow by 1 month (r = 0.46, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.53, n = 545 months). Flood timing is a broad late-winter mode with no drift across decades (Imboden annual peaks mean date 24 Feb, R = 0.49, n = 89), and recession constants show no trend (Hardy median k 14 days, Sen slope 0.0618 days/yr (95% CI -0.215 to 0.401); MK z=0.50, p=0.620; n=16; Mammoth Spring 188 days, Sen slope 0.216 days/yr (95% CI -1.03 to 1.7); MK z=0.41, p=0.681; n=80). No conclusion changed when provisional data were excluded.

2 Setting

  • River gauge. USGS 07069305 Spring River at Hardy, AR (NWS HDYA4). Daily discharge WY 2002–present; 15-min stage from 2007-10-01; 24 annual peaks (WY 2002–2025). There is no USGS daily-stage product at Hardy; daily stage is the daily maximum of the instantaneous record.
  • Long flood record. USGS 07069500 Spring River at Imboden, AR, downstream: daily discharge from 1936 and 89 annual peaks (WY 1937–2025 in the NWIS peak file).
  • Spring. USGS 07069190 Mammoth Spring at Mammoth Spring, AR: the vent gauge, daily discharge from 1981-02-25 with no gaps > 7 days. It carries the 1981+ base-flow record; Hardy is the WY 2002+ series.
  • Recharge basin. No dye-trace delineation was obtained. The basin is approximated as a 30 km buffer around West Plains, MO (36.744° N, 91.852° W); basin precipitation is the PRISM 4 km grid mean over that box. Station series: USC00238880 West Plains COOP (1981+ in this build) and KUNO West Plains ASOS (1998-04+).
  • Flood categories (NWS HDYA4). Action 8 ft, minor 10 ft, moderate 14 ft, major 16 ft. Record crest 29.0 ft on 1982-12-03 (flow not reported), before the systematic Hardy record.
  • Conventions. Water year (Oct–Sep) for hydrologic statistics; calendar year for precipitation totals; recharge season Sep–Feb. No interpolation across gaps > 7 days. Every analysis is run on all data and on approved-only data; any conclusion that changes is flagged.

3 Data and QA

Full gap maps, cross-check residuals and the deferred QA items are in docs/qa_report.md.

  • Hardy discharge has no gaps > 7 days; Imboden has two (1995–2001, 2015–2016) that are excluded, not filled. Hardy daily-max stage has two short 2014 gaps (13 and 9 days).
  • Hardy vs Imboden log-ratio cross-check: 8,666 overlap days, 63 days with |z| > 4 (0.73%), concentrated on flood rise/fall days where the two gauges are out of phase.
  • Precipitation: USC00238880 has np.int64(32) gaps > 7 days; KUNO starts 1998-04. Daily KUNO/COOP correlation is 0.42 because the COOP observation day ends ~7 AM; on monthly totals r = 0.86, ratio COOP/KUNO = 1.07, n = 282 months, so the two stations agree and the daily discrepancy is an observation-time artifact.
  • Provisional data: Hardy and Mammoth discharge are provisional from 2026-04-09; every result below was recomputed on approved-only data and none changed.

4 Base-flow regime

Thesis: base flow tracks antecedent precipitation; there is no detectable structural decline, and the visible drop in the stage floor is mostly rating drift.

4.1 Low-flow trend and attribution (Q1)

Predictors are strictly antecedent to each water year’s min7 window: basin precipitation over the 365 days ending the day before the window, the 365 days before that, and mean ONI over the 6 months ending the month before. Incomplete water years are excluded. Model: OLS log(min7) ~ p_trailing + p_trailing_prev + ONI (HC3 SEs); the residual is trend-tested (Mann-Kendall, Sen slope with Gilbert CI).

  • Mammoth (1981+, the primary series): raw min7 is flat (Sen slope 0.000319 log-cfs/yr (95% CI -0.00376 to 0.00357); MK z=0.13, p=0.897; n=42); the residual after climate is Sen slope -0.00222 log-cfs/yr (95% CI -0.00497 to 0.000453); MK z=-1.71, p=0.087; n=42 — a point estimate of -2.2% per decade with a CI spanning zero.
  • Hardy (WY 2002+): raw min7 rises (Sen slope 0.023 log-cfs/yr (95% CI 0.00736 to 0.0361); MK z=3.05, p=0.002; n=24; Pettitt step after WY 2013, p = 0.013), but trailing-365-day precipitation carries the signal (coefficient 0.023 log-cfs per inch, 95% CI 0.0097 to 0.0363); the residual trend CI includes zero.
  • Base-flow index (gap-segmented Eckhardt; Lyne-Hollick as check) has no trend: Mammoth Sen slope 2.3e-05 BFI/yr (95% CI -4.6e-05 to 0.00012); MK z=0.75, p=0.451; n=45; Hardy Sen slope 0.0013 BFI/yr (95% CI -0.0014 to 0.0038); MK z=1.10, p=0.272; n=25.

Limitation: Hardy n = 24 water years; the ONI coefficient is not resolved at either gauge; basin precipitation is a 30 km buffer, not a traced recharge polygon.

4.2 Rating drift (Q5)

Stage at a fixed discharge from 666,986 matched 15-min (stage, discharge) pairs: a local log-linear fit (stage = a + b·log10 Q over pairs within ±20 % of the target) per water year, evaluated at 400 and 1000 cfs.

  • Stage at 400 cfs: Sen slope -0.00791 ft/yr (95% CI -0.0132 to -0.00491); MK z=-4.41, p=0.000; n=19. Stage at 1000 cfs: Sen slope -0.0187 ft/yr (95% CI -0.0214 to -0.0157); MK z=-5.46, p=0.000; n=19 — about 0.19 ft per decade of channel-bed lowering or rating shift at moderate flow, unrelated to discharge.
  • Shifts across individual ≥16 ft events (±365-day windows) range -0.18 to +0.02 ft; the drift is gradual rather than event-stepped.

Limitation: USGS rating-shift and datum history was not obtained; the drift is inferred from IV pairs only and is provisional until the official record is compared.

4.2.1 Stage–discharge relationship

Across the 666,986 matched pairs, log10 stage and log10 discharge correlate at Pearson r = 0.969 (Spearman ρ = 0.963); the annual-peak log-log fit used in §9 is log10 Q = 1.954 + 2.215·log10 H (R² = 0.991, n = 24 peaks).

  • The paddling range lives inside about 2.0 ft of stage: the 5th to 95th percentile of daily discharge (328–2,859 cfs) spans 2.87–4.91 ft on the recent rating, and the median day (690 cfs) reads 3.23 ft.
  • The same stage carries more water now than the record-wide median at the low end: at 3.0–4.0 ft the recent median discharge is +8 to +18 % above the whole-record value, the lookup-table expression of the §4.2 drift; above 6 ft the two agree within 1 %.

4.3 Post-flood base flow (Q4)

For each ≥16 ft event, mean Eckhardt base flow over 6 months starting 30 days after the event is compared with the same calendar window in the 3 non-flood years closest in standardized distance on post-window precipitation and antecedent (90-day) base flow.

  • Mean difference: Mammoth +27.5% (bootstrap 95% CI 19.8 to 42; n = 6 events, 15 unique control years); Hardy +22.9% (CI 12.6 to 35.1; n = 6, 11 controls). Every event’s difference is positive. The hypothesis that major floods suppress recharge is not supported; the sign is opposite.

Limitation: the CI reflects event-to-event variation only; matching uncertainty and control-year reuse are not propagated. Descriptive, not causal.

5 Flood regime

Thesis: flood frequency at Hardy and Imboden is stationary within the resolving power of the record; return periods beyond ~50 yr are extrapolation.

5.1 Flood frequency (Q8)

Log-Pearson III by method of moments with Bulletin 17B weighted skew (regional skew -0.2, approximate), Grubbs-Beck low-outlier screen flagging but not dropping, and a 2,000-resample nonparametric bootstrap for the 5–95 % interval. Not EMA; the 1982 crest is not in the fit.

  • Hardy 10-yr flood 62,391 cfs (44,282–79,486); 100-yr 133,946 cfs (87,021–179,736), a 69%-wide interval relative to the estimate. Replacing weighted skew with station skew moves the Hardy 100-yr estimate to 135,408 cfs (+1.1%).

5.2 Stationarity (Q2)

  • Hardy annual peaks: Sen slope 0.00125 log10-cfs/yr (95% CI -0.0232 to 0.03); MK z=0.17, p=0.862; n=24; Pettitt after WY 2011.
  • Imboden annual peaks: Sen slope 0.00112 log10-cfs/yr (95% CI -0.00123 to 0.00406); MK z=0.94, p=0.346; n=89; Pettitt after WY 2005.
  • Imboden LP3 split at WY 2008: 10-yr quantile 63,943 cfs (51,676–79,094, n = 71) before vs 95,546 cfs (64,510–126,275, n = 18) after; intervals overlap: yes.
  • Rule: “non-stationary” requires both a trend CI excluding zero and non-overlapping split-period 10-yr CIs. Verdict: no detectable change in flood frequency.. The post-2008 point estimate is higher; the n = 18 record cannot distinguish it from sampling variation.

5.3 Partial-duration series and threshold counts

Events are daily-max IV stage exceedances with 7-day declustering, complete water years 2008–2025 (n = 18).

  • ≥16 ft: 6 events, 0.33/yr, dispersion 1.1 (p = 0.78); count trend -0 events/yr (95% CI -0 to -0); MK z=-1.27, p=0.204; n=18. Approved-only counts are identical.

5.4 Inter-arrival of major floods (Q6)

Events (annual-peak file before WY 2008; declustered daily-max stage after): 2006-09-23, 2008-03-19, 2008-04-10, 2009-10-30, 2011-04-26, 2017-04-30, 2025-04-05.

CV ≈ 1 and bootstrap p = 0.47 (n = 7) are the exponential signature: the ~4-yr cadence is modal, not periodic. A spectral check on n = 7 events is not informative and was not run.

5.5 Quiet year after a major flood (Q7)

P(annual peak < 8 ft | prior WY had a ≥16 ft event) = 0 vs base rate 0.08; difference -0.08 (Clopper-Pearson exact 95 % bounds -0.08 to +0.44); permutation p = 1; n_major = 5, n_years = 24. No support for the pattern; the CI is the honest statement of power.

5.6 Antecedent conditions

The two largest stage events (2011-04-26, 12.5 in prior) and the driest antecedent case (2003-11-18, 2.0 in) both produced ≥14 ft peaks; antecedent wetness is not a necessary condition for a major flood on this karst system, with n = 9.

6 Precipitation regime

Thesis: basin-mean precipitation has become wetter and more intense over 1981–2025, but the Sep–Feb recharge-season total has not changed; station tests are low-power.

Indices are calendar-year: total, Sep–Feb recharge-season total, growing-season total, wet-day counts at 0.5/1/2 in, max 1- and 3-day totals, top-5-day fraction, and SDII. Trend: Sen slope per decade with 95 % CI, Mann-Kendall, Benjamini-Hochberg across the 10 indices per series; years with < 90 % daily coverage are excluded.

  • Basin (PRISM 30 km mean, n = 45 years): 9/10 indices BH-significant. Annual total +2.41 in/decade (95 % CI 0.35 to 4.5; mean 47.7 in); days ≥ 1 in +1.45/decade (CI 0.71 to 2.3); max 1-day +0.28 in/decade (CI 0.097 to 0.53); SDII +0.0347 in/wet-day/decade (CI 0.022 to 0.049).
  • Recharge season (Sep–Feb, 46% of the annual mean): -0.0177 in/decade (CI -1.3 to 1.2, n = 44). The wetting is a growing-season signal.
  • Stations: USC00238880 0/10 significant (n = 34; max 3-day +0.508 in/decade, CI 0.072 to 0.91, p_BH = 0.13); KUNO 1/10 (SDII +0.0634, CI 0.033 to 0.09, n = 27). USC00238880 fails the coverage gate in 11 years, 10 of them in 2011–2021 (2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021), which removes most of the recent wet decade from the station test; its null is low power, not evidence against the basin trend.

Limitation: PRISM is a 4 km grid mean (smoother extremes by construction) and station gaps enter it only through interpolation; the COOP record before 1981 is not yet pulled; precipitation carries no approval flag, so the all/approved rule does not apply here.

6.1 Seasonality and recession

Thesis: floods arrive in late winter–early spring at every gauge and in every decade with enough events to test, and the timing has not drifted; post-peak recession is fast at Hardy (k ≈ 14 days) and slow at Mammoth Spring (k ≈ 188 days), and neither constant trends with water year.

Peak timing is the circular mean of day-of-year per calendar decade; R is the mean resultant length (0 = uniform through the year, 1 = every peak on the same day); the Rayleigh test is of uniformity (Zar approximation, adequate for n ≥ 3, blank below). Decades are calendar decades, so the first row of each series is partial.

  • Whole series: Imboden annual peaks n = 89, mean date 24 Feb, R = 0.49, Rayleigh p = 0.0000; Hardy annual peaks n = 24, mean date 03 Mar, R = 0.43, Rayleigh p = 0.0115; Hardy POT ≥ 10 ft events n = 17, mean date 03 Mar, R = 0.53, Rayleigh p = 0.0062. All three reject uniformity; R ≈ 0.4–0.5 means a broad late-winter mode, not a narrow one.
  • Decades: Imboden decade means range from 16 Jan (2000–2009) to 09 Apr (1960–1969) with no monotone ordering across the 10 decades; the 2020s rows (n = 6–7) sit inside the spread of earlier decades. Per-decade Rayleigh tests at n ≤ 11 have little power and are reported, not interpreted.

Recession constant k (days) is from OLS ln q = a − t/k on each recession run after the quickflow crest (Hardy: min peak 10,000 cfs, skip 3 days, ≥10-day runs, ≤2% daily rise; Mammoth Spring: min peak 488 cfs, skip 3 days, ≥10-day runs, ≤2% daily rise); runs are extracted only within gap-free segments. Trend: Mann-Kendall / Sen on k vs water year of the peak, recomputed here from the per-event tables.

  • Hardy: 16 events (k fitted for 16), median k 13.9 days (IQR 13.0–17.4), median r² 0.953. Trend Sen slope 0.0618 days/yr (95% CI -0.215 to 0.401); MK z=0.50, p=0.620; n=16. Pettitt change-point after 2015-12-28 (WY 2016; K = 42, p = 0.176) — not significant.
  • Mammoth Spring: 81 events (k fitted for 80), median k 188.0 days (IQR 150.0–231.5), median r² 0.978. Trend Sen slope 0.216 days/yr (95% CI -1.03 to 1.7); MK z=0.41, p=0.681; n=80. Pettitt after 2016-06-05 (WY 2016; K = 336, p = 0.541) — not significant. The spring drains an order of magnitude more slowly than the river: a Hardy crest is back on its base-flow floor in weeks, the Mammoth response persists for months (§7 lag structure).
  • Approved-only: identical event sets and identical trends — no qualifying peak falls in the provisional period (from 2026-04-09); recession runs were re-extracted within approved-only gap-free segments.

Limitation: Hardy POT events use daily-max IV stage, an upper bound relative to a daily-mean product; k depends on the min-peak and skip choices and a single-exponential fit ignores multi-store behaviour (r² per event in the tables); the k trend treats each event as a sample although events cluster within wet years, so n overstates independence; the Rayleigh test is of uniformity only, so a bimodal spring/autumn pattern can give low R without being uniform; master curves are unweighted medians and the late IQR band rests on few long runs.

7 Coupling

Monthly anomalies (climatology removed; log flow) of basin precipitation vs Mammoth Spring discharge, lags 0–12 months, 1000-resample 12-month block bootstrap for the CI.

  • Response peaks at lag 1 month: r = 0.46 (95 % CI 0.42 to 0.53, n = 545), vs r = 0.3 at lag 0. Correlation decays to a CI including zero by lag 8: the spring integrates roughly two seasons of rainfall, with the bulk of the response inside one to three months.
  • Approved-only flow: lag 1, r = 0.47 (CI 0.42 to 0.53, n = 541) — unchanged.
  • Spring → river: Hardy min7 is set by Mammoth base flow plus tributary inflow; the Hardy attribution model (§4.1) uses the same trailing-365-day precipitation window and reaches R² = 0.47.

Limitation: the block bootstrap preserves within-year serial correlation but not dependence across block boundaries, so the CI is mildly optimistic. The per-event recession constants behind this lag structure are in §6.1.

8 Synthesis

  • What changed. Basin precipitation: wetter and more intense in 9 of 10 indices, concentrated in the growing season. Hardy stage at fixed discharge: 0.19 ft/decade lower at 1000 cfs.
  • What did not. Non-climatic base flow at either gauge; BFI; flood magnitude and frequency; recharge-season precipitation; the inter-arrival process of major floods; flood timing within the year and the recession constants at both gauges.
  • What is uncertain. Return periods beyond ~50 yr (Hardy n = 24); the post-2008 Imboden shift (higher point estimate, n = 18); the post-flood base-flow gain (n = 6 events, matching uncertainty not propagated); everything that depends on the unobtained USGS rating history.
  • Sensitivity: no result changed between all and approved-only data (Phase 4–7 reports, every item; the Phase 7 recession event sets are identical because no qualifying peak is provisional).

9 Practical thresholds

Stage→flow: log10 Q = 1.954 + 2.215·log10 H (R² = 0.991, n = 24 annual-peak pairs). Rating drift (§4.2) propagates into this mapping.

Band Stage at Hardy Basis Expected recurrence
Paddling, low below the 400 cfs stage (2.95 ft in WY 2026) stage-at-flow fit, drifting 0.08 ft/decade typical late-summer base flow (min7 348 cfs median WY 2002–2025)
Paddling, runnable 400–1000 cfs (2.95–3.56 ft) stage-at-flow fit most of the year; Mammoth supplies ≥ 174 cfs (record min7)
Action / bank-full 8–10 ft (9,001–14,756 cfs) NWS action/minor 1.2–1.4 yr LP3; 2.5 declustered ≥8 ft events per year
Flood exposure, moderate 14–16 ft (31,093–41,795 cfs) NWS moderate/major 2.9–4.5 yr LP3 (empirical 2.7–4)
Flood exposure, major 20–23 ft (68,516–93,380 cfs) 2008/2025 tier 12.5–29 yr LP3; 5 NWS crests ≥ 20 ft in 1982–2025
Stage → flow lookup 3.0–14.0 ft in Table 6; median day 3.23 ft = 690 cfs ±0.05 ft bands on 666,986 IV pairs (§4.2.1) use the recent column below 6 ft; whole-record above
Monitoring alert basin precipitation anomaly this month → Mammoth flow next month (r = 0.46); any ≥8 ft rise → recheck stage-at-flow drift §7, §4.2 —

The practical number for 22+ ft is the empirical rate: 3 annual peaks ≥ 20 ft in 24 water years plus the 1982 crest outside the systematic record; the LP3 29 yr at 23 ft carries the full width of the n = 24 bootstrap band.

10 Limitations and next steps

Data and record length

  • Hardy discharge is WY 2002+ (n ≤ 24 for low-flow statistics, 24 annual peaks); Mammoth Spring (1981+) carries the long base-flow record and Imboden (WY 1937+) the long flood record. Return periods beyond ~50 yr are extrapolation — the CIs say so.
  • Hardy daily stage is the daily maximum of IV readings (WY 2008+); threshold-day counts and POT events are an upper bound relative to a daily-mean product.
  • The 1982 29.0 ft crest predates the Hardy record and is reported as a historical exceedance only, not fitted.
  • COOP USC00238880 has np.int64(32) gaps > 7 days and fails coverage in 11 index years; its 1948–1980 record was not pulled in this build (ACIS cache keyed on station id). KUNO begins 1998-04.

Unobtained inputs (open items from the plan)

  • USGS rating-shift, measurement and datum history for Hardy: Q5 and the stage↔︎flow mapping in Q8 rest on IV-derived stage-at-flow and a log-log fit to 24 annual-peak pairs, and are provisional until compared with the official record.
  • Regional skew: -0.2 is the Bulletin 17B Plate I approximation; the Arkansas/Missouri regional-skew study value and an EMA (B17C, PeakFQ) fit with the 1982 crest as a historical peak remain to be done.
  • Recharge-basin polygon: 30 km West Plains buffer, not a dye-traced delineation.

Methods

  • LP3 is method-of-moments with weighted skew, not EMA; low outliers are flagged but retained without a conditional-probability adjustment.
  • Q4 n = 6 events; the bootstrap CI excludes matching uncertainty and control-year reuse (descriptive, not causal). BFImax is fixed rather than fitted; no linear-reservoir attribution.
  • Q6 spectral check not run (n = 7 events; not informative). Q7 has n_major = 5.
  • Lag-correlation block bootstrap is mildly optimistic across block boundaries.
  • Review overrules (docs/review_phase4-6.md): complete-WY selection uses the series end date only (no interior year-long stage gaps exist); Q4 precipitation windows have no coverage gate (PRISM basin series is complete).
  • Seasonality (§6.1): Hardy POT event dates are the day of the declustered daily-max IV stage; the Rayleigh test is of uniformity only (a bimodal spring/autumn pattern can give low R without being uniform); Imboden annual peaks in NWIS begin WY 1937, so the 1930s row is partial and earlier decades are absent; per-decade tests at n ≤ 11 are low power.
  • Recession (§6.1): k depends on the min-peak (Hardy 10,000 cfs; Mammoth 488 cfs, the 90 % quantile of its DV) and 3-day skip choices; a single-exponential fit ignores multi-store behaviour; the k trend treats each event as a sample although events cluster within wet years, so n overstates independence; master curves are unweighted medians truncated at the last day reached by ≥ 3 runs, and the late IQR band rests on few long runs.

Next steps: obtain the USGS rating history and regional skew; backfill COOP 1948–1980; EMA fit with historical information; Phase 8 adversarial review of the conclusions.

11.4 Review record

Independent adversarial review of Phases 4–6 (two Codex passes, 2026-08-25; 9 + 3 blocking findings, all fixed or explicitly overruled): docs/review_phase4-6.md. Material effects: Q1 predictors made strictly antecedent (Hardy residual trend lost significance); LP3 retains low outliers by default; basin recharge-season trend went to ~0 once the coverage gate was corrected.
